theories.description: General theory: anxiety about academic demands does not stay confined to study time but intrudes into rest and leisure, and this persistent mental occupation drains energy so that distress co-occurs with depletion. Anxiety and exhaustion are two faces of one process rather than independent problems.
theories.name: Intrusive anxiety depletes capacity (general)
negative_experiments: If intrusion and depletion statements never co-occur in the same held-out chunk, the theory is contradicted.
If chunks with no rest-time intrusion show equal or higher depletion, the depletion route is contradicted.
new_predictions_likely: Held-out narratives containing intrusion statements (worry during rest) will mention depletion statements more often than narratives without intrusion.
Co-occurrence of anxiety and exhaustion terms will be higher in the same chunk than in independently sampled chunks.
new_predictions_unknown: Whether intrusion precedes depletion or depletion produces the subjective sense of inability to disconnect cannot be decided cross-sectionally.

evidence.summary: I tried to watch a show after dinner, but I kept thinking about the assignment I still haven’t finished. Even when I’m supposed to be relaxing, my mind is just running through deadlines and grades.
I went out to eat with my family, but I was distracted the whole time worrying about my grades and the project due next week. Even my free time feels occupied by school.
When I’m not studying, I’m still mentally studying, planning, or worrying. It’s like school has taken over all my downtime.

theory_statements.law: When academic worry persists, it co-occurs with feelings of being unable to mentally disconnect, and both together travel with reports of depletion.
theory_statements.scope: Students reporting school-related stress in narrative form; expected to fail where academic demands are genuinely finished or externalized and no longer mentally active.

evidence.summary: Schoolwork doesn’t feel meaningful anymore, so I procrastinate until it’s almost too late. I’m scared of failing, but I’m also tired of caring so much.

theory_statements.law: Students who report fear of failing alongside reduced meaning also report being tired of caring, so anxiety and depletion are expressed in the same accounts.
theory_statements.scope: Applicable to middle-to-late-stage burnout where meaning has eroded; not expected at early burnout when anxiety is present but energy is intact.

unaccounted_evidence.summary: I feel buried under assignments from every class, and no matter how much I work, the pile never seems to get smaller. It makes me feel like I’m always behind before I even start.
It’s weird because I used to like learning, and now I can barely care enough to open my notebook. Schoolwork has become something I go through automatically.
I try to stay on top of everything, but I keep making mistakes and it’s embarrassing. I feel weaker and less capable than the other students.

theories.description: General theory: interpreting academic struggle as evidence of personal inadequacy sustains effortful self-monitoring, embarrassment, and comparison, which are energetically costly; over time this appraisal-driven monitoring contributes to depletion and eroded confidence as mutually reinforcing states.
theories.name: Self-appraisal drain (general)
negative_experiments: If self-inadequacy framing never co-occurs with depletion statements in the held-out partition, the drain claim is contradicted.
If depletion statements appear equally often with external-cause and self-cause framings, the appraisal-specific route is weakened.
new_predictions_likely: Held-out chunks containing self-inadequacy framing (weaker, less capable, embarrassment) will co-mention depletion more than chunks with external-cause framing.
new_predictions_unknown: Whether the appraisal loop is a cause of depletion or a by-product of it cannot be settled with cross-sectional narrative data.

evidence.summary: I try to stay on top of everything, but I keep making mistakes and it’s embarrassing. I feel weaker and less capable than the other students.

theory_statements.law: Students who frame mistakes and difficulties as evidence of being less capable than peers report co-occurring embarrassment and weakened self-assessment, indicating an active appraisal-monitoring loop.
theory_statements.scope: Students in peer-visible academic settings where comparison is possible; not expected where performance feedback is absent or de-identified.

evidence.summary: Schoolwork doesn’t feel meaningful anymore, so I procrastinate until it’s almost too late. I’m scared of failing, but I’m also tired of caring so much.
It’s weird because I used to like learning, and now I can barely care enough to open my notebook. Schoolwork has become something I go through automatically.

theory_statements.law: Sustained self-monitoring and meaning erosion co-occur with exhaustion and automatic low-effort engagement, so appraisal-driven effort contributes to depletion.
theory_statements.scope: Late-stage burnout where meaning has eroded; early burnout may show monitoring without full depletion.

I went out to eat with my family, but I was distracted the whole time worrying about my grades and the project due next week. Even my free time feels occupied by school.

theories.description: Specific theory: the key signature of academic anxiety in school burnout is not worry during study but worry during non-study time; this rest-time intrusion is the channel through which anxiety becomes experienced as burden rather than as effort, and it predicts co-occurring depletion in the same narrative chunk.
theories.name: Rest-time intrusion as the primary distress channel (specific)
negative_experiments: If high-distress chunks rarely mention rest-time intrusion, this theory is contradicted.
If study-time worry alone predicts depletion as well as rest-time intrusion, the specific channel claim is contradicted.
new_predictions_likely: In the held-out partition, rest-time intrusion statements will appear in a majority of high-distress chunks.
Rest-time intrusion will be a better marker of co-occurring depletion than study-time worry.
new_predictions_unknown: Whether rest-time intrusion is a symptom or a cause of the broader burnout syndrome remains undetermined.

evidence.summary: I tried to watch a show after dinner, but I kept thinking about the assignment I still haven’t finished. Even when I’m supposed to be relaxing, my mind is just running through deadlines and grades.
I went out to eat with my family, but I was distracted the whole time worrying about my grades and the project due next week. Even my free time feels occupied by school.
When I’m not studying, I’m still mentally studying, planning, or worrying. It’s like school has taken over all my downtime.

theory_statements.law: Anxiety described as intruding into designated rest or leisure time marks the transition from productive worry to burden, and is the dominant anxiety form in burnout narratives.
theory_statements.scope: Students in sustained academic pressure; not expected among students with clearly separated study and leisure routines.

evidence.summary: Schoolwork doesn’t feel meaningful anymore, so I procrastinate until it’s almost too late. I’m scared of failing, but I’m also tired of caring so much.
It’s weird because I used to like learning, and now I can barely care enough to open my notebook. Schoolwork has become something I go through automatically.

theory_statements.law: Chunks that name rest as invaded also name depletion, because the inability to recover is what students report as exhaustion.
theory_statements.scope: Cross-sectional narratives; does not apply to acute single-deadline stress where rest is preserved.

theories.description: Specific theory: in school burnout, the collapse of meaning for schoolwork is the pivotal event; once schoolwork no longer feels meaningful, students shift into automatic, low-investment engagement, which reads as exhaustion and co-occurs with reduced anxiety about outcomes because caring itself has dropped.
theories.name: Meaning collapse precedes automatic engagement (specific)
negative_experiments: If meaning-loss statements are rare in high-distress chunks, this theory is contradicted.
If meaning loss is not differentially associated with automatic engagement versus workload pressure, the pivotal-event claim is weakened.
new_predictions_likely: Held-out chunks reporting loss of meaning will co-mention automatic or barely-caring engagement more than chunks reporting only workload pressure.
new_predictions_unknown: Whether meaning collapse is reversible and whether reversed meaning predicts recovery of engagement is not testable on this corpus.

evidence.summary: It’s weird because I used to like learning, and now I can barely care enough to open my notebook. Schoolwork has become something I go through automatically.

theory_statements.law: Loss of meaning for schoolwork appears before or alongside automatic low-effort engagement and is reported together with reduced investment.
theory_statements.scope: Late-stage burnout; not expected in early burnout where meaning is intact and effort is still high.

evidence.summary: Schoolwork doesn’t feel meaningful anymore, so I procrastinate until it’s almost too late. I’m scared of failing, but I’m also tired of caring so much.

theory_statements.law: As meaning collapses, fear of failure remains but is paired with tiredness of caring, so the distress profile shifts from pure anxiety to mixed anxiety-plus-depletion.
theory_statements.scope: Applies to students who previously cared about outcomes; not expected where anxiety is absent from the start.
